title: Consideration releases familiar dependence

captions.emotions: Feeling attachment and fear of release

meaning: Your care can remain considerate when ending unnecessary help creates fear of losing importance without creating another concealed debt.
text: Even a considerate ending of help can touch a familiar sense of being needed. In the physical position of Anahata, Death expresses care through ending an exhausted support pattern and moving towards other involvement. Strength in energy brings a wish to meet vulnerability gently without suppressing it through personal forcefulness. The Devil in emotions offers attachment, fear of release and the grip of former dependence. Accepted independence may feel tender while a changed role creates worry. Care preserves freedom when worry becomes neither a condition of someone’s availability nor grounds to restore an unnecessary service.

For example, one person has long helped the other choose clothes for every personal outing. You now end that habit without ridiculing former doubts or inspecting new choices unasked. **A considerate ending does not require preserving dependence for warmth.** One question remains possible, while attention does not disappear with a service. A meeting can be wanted directly without reminders of how often help was given.

Fear of losing a role can turn gentleness into concealed restraint: help is no longer compulsory, but declining it causes resentment. Alternatively, independence rejects every kind response. Warmth preserves a clear distinction between a concrete request and permanent debt. A suggestion can be accepted and earlier efforts valued while acting independently, without proving closeness through continuing an old vulnerability.
